goals: Mechanistic: quantify how Naches partitions incoming water between surface runoff (QOVER) and recharge/subsurface drainage (QDRAI), and how that split varies with elevation-driven climate and soil texture
Validation: check simulated snow (SWE) and water-table depth against in-domain observations

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM natively produces the runoff (QOVER) and recharge/drainage (QDRAI) partitioning terms; the question is a per-column water-balance question, well suited to stratified 1-D sampling. Naches is in CONUS so NLDAS resolves orographic forcing.

answerable: Runoff vs recharge partitioning (QOVER vs QDRAI) per column, given WTD warm start + spin-up
Soil-texture control on infiltration/runoff split (SSURGO lever)
Elevation-as-climate control on partitioning, to ~12 km resolution (NLDAS orographic precip/phase)
Water-table-depth validation vs USGS wells (co-located, after warm start)

not_answerable.aspect: Basin-integrated streamflow vs USGS stream gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing/aggregation; there is no native integrated streamflow to compare against a gauge

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km terrain effects on snow/precip (ridgetop SWE, fine-scale rain-snow line)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS is ~12 km with no within-cell lapse rate; ridgetop SWE will be underestimated

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 dominant soil textures = 6 to span the driver cross-product, plus +2 replicates in the mid/rain-snow-transition band where precip-phase and thus the runoff/recharge split is most sensitive. This matches the 'handful' request while resolving both drivers.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in the rain-snow transition (mid elevation) where melt timing controls partitioning; sample valley bottoms where recharge/drainage dominates and where USGS wells exist; include high-elevation snow columns to capture the snowmelt-driven end member. Prefer the dominant SSURGO class within each elevation band.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 extra columns in the mid band to cover both soil textures and capture within-band sensitivity of the melt-driven split

sampling_plan.reason: Low-elevation, high-infiltration end member where recharge/drainage should dominate over surface runoff
Low-elevation runoff-prone soil to contrast infiltration-limited vs texture-limited partitioning at the basin outlet zone
Most climate-sensitive band; coarse soil isolates melt-driven recharge where infiltration capacity is high (replicated for sensitivity)
Melt-season runoff generation on runoff-prone soils; the band where partitioning is expected to shift most (replicated)
Snow-dominated end member: delayed melt input, tests snowmelt-driven recharge vs runoff
High-elevation runoff-prone soil to bound the snowmelt runoff response

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place/associate validation columns at the 6 SNOTEL elevations; compare peak-SWE and melt-out timing
validation_design.metric: bias, RMSE on peak SWE; timing error on melt-out

validation_design.comparison: co-located — compare after Fan-2013 WTD warm start + spin-up; expect some drift (1-D vs lateral equilibrium) which is itself a result
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well density in HUC 17030002

validation_design.comparison: NOT comparable without routing/aggregation — flagged as a gap, not validated here

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing (nearest 12 km cell), native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up

requires_capabilities.why: Recharge and water table are slow states; cold-start default 8.8 m WTD makes QDRAI an initialization artifact
requires_capabilities.blocks: credible recharge partitioning and WTD validation

requires_capabilities.why: Single-column ELM produces no integrated streamflow
NLDAS 12 km averages terrain; ridgetop snow/precip under-resolved
requires_capabilities.blocks: fine-scale snow/rain-snow-line accuracy at high elevation

requires_capabilities.why: To realize elevation bands into concrete points
To assign coarse/fine soil classes per column
To pin and score co-located validation

assumptions: Naches (WA) lies within CONUS NLDAS-2 coverage, so orographic precip/temperature vary across columns
Dominant SSURGO textures reduce reasonably to a coarse vs fine contrast per elevation band
USGS wells exist within the HUC; exact count/depths unknown until ingest
Recharge is interpreted as ELM subsurface drainage QDRAI; runoff as QOVER
Fan-2013 warm start is acceptable despite expected 1-D vs lateral-equilibrium drift
open_questions: How many USGS wells fall inside HUC 17030002 and at what depths (sets WTD validation N)?
Which forcing years / spin-up length are desired (affects cost at NLDAS ~30 min/sim-yr/column)?
Is a future routing/aggregation step planned so stream gauges can be used?
Should analysis focus on long-term mean partitioning or interannual/seasonal (wet vs dry year) variation?
